subject: Capacity planning: US/EU/APAC dedicated pools for Quantech & Atlas deals
messages:
From: Simon Park <simon@quantech.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@quantech.ai
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Q3 capacity ask — US + EU dedicated pools

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving to a pilot with a commercial launch target in early Q3 and need to lock down dedicated capacity sizing and a mutual action plan. High-level forecast attached (quantech-q3-forecast.csv). Key points: 

- Peak sustained inference load: ~120 RPS for small responses (avg 80 tokens) across our US customers, expected to be 60-70% of traffic.
- Embedding workload (batch embed jobs): bursty, ~10 concurrent jobs at 2k vectors each during nightly windows.
- EU presence: we expect 30% of inference traffic in EU with strict latency SLOs (p95 < 200ms).
- APAC: low initial traffic but we need regional failover for compliance for one customer (will be cold).

Can you recommend a region-specific dedicated pool plan (frac reserved vs burst), rough GPU counts by region, and an estimate of cost uplift for reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go? We need this for our procurement review by 6/18.

Also looping procurement for contract lead time (procurement@quantech.ai).

Thanks,
Simon
Head of Platform
Quantech

Attachment: quantech-q3-forecast.csv (csv, 28KB)
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Simon Park <simon@quantech.ai>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@quantech.ai
Date: 2026-06-10T13:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Q3 capacity ask — US + EU dedicated pools

Simon — thanks for the forecast and context. We can support this, but want to make a few recommended trade-offs so procurement and infra have clear asks. High-level recommendation attached (initial-sizing-proposal.xlsx). TL;DR proposal: 

- US (primary): 8 A100-equivalent GPU slots in a reserved pool, with an additional 4-GPU burst tranche (burst on-demand) for launch spikes.
- EU (local region): 5 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (to meet latency SLOs) with 2-GPU burst for scheduled load peaks.
- APAC (failover): 1-2 GPUs reserved for compliance standby; can be shared across customers with strict routing policy.

Rationale and notes: 
- The US pool sizing targets the 120 RPS steady inference requirement assuming batching efficiencies and KV-cache hit rate of ~30%. If cache hit is lower we will need an additional ~15-25% headroom.
- EU requires higher reserved ratio due to cross-border restrictions and p95 latency target; burst alone won't reliably meet p95 spike constraints.
- We recommend a staged ramp: provision reserved pools at 70% of the final target for launch (canary traffic), then enable burst capacity for immediate headroom, and schedule a 30-day ramp to full reserved commit tied to usage metrics.
- Autoscaling policy: prefer quick ramping of burst GPUs for embedding batch windows; reserve GPUs remain pinned for low-latency inference.

Open asks for you/procurement: 
1) Confirm token mix (percent long vs short responses) — affects GPU usage.
2) Confirm acceptable committed term (monthly vs annual) — we can model price delta.
3) Any required peak concurrency for embedding jobs (we assumed 10 concurrent).

Next steps: if you sign off on the attached numbers I will loop infra (karthik) for provisioning timeline and finance for a provisional quote.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Attachment: initial-sizing-proposal.xlsx (xlsx, 64KB)
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-11T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Q3 capacity ask — US + EU dedicated pools

Looping in a quick internal ops take.

Grace — the numbers above are reasonable but I recommend the following tactical changes before we give procurement a final quote: 
- Shift 1 reserved GPU from APAC to EU for initial launch (APAC can be served via burst/backfill from nearby region for the first 60 days). That gives EU 6 reserved GPUs to absorb early variability and meet p95 targets.
- For Quantech's embedding window, prefer pre-warmed burst instances (short-lived) rather than reserving dedicated GPUs for nightly batches; this reduces committed cost.
- Add a canary deployment: route 10% of traffic to the reserved EU pool for 7 days, monitor p95 and error rates (Jira: SUP-3421).

Cost note: moving one GPU reserved from APAC->EU increases EU committed cost but reduces risk of SLA breach. I've added a quick cost delta in our sizing sheet.

Marcus Lin
Head of Deal Operations — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Related: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SUP-3421
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Simon Park <simon@quantech.ai>, lina.choi@atlas-ai.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@quantech.ai
Date: 2026-06-12T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Q3 capacity ask — US + EU dedicated pools

Simon/Lina — following internal alignment we can proceed with the adjusted plan. Summary decision and next steps: 

1) Provisioning: reserve 8 GPUs (US), 6 GPUs (EU), 1 GPU (APAC standby). Burst tranche: US +4, EU +2.
2) Canary & ramp: route 10% traffic to EU reserved pool for 7 days (SUP-3421). If metrics look good, increase to 70% reserved utilization over 30 days.
3) Embedding: use pre-warmed burst instances for nightly jobs; do not reserve GPUs for embed bursts initially.
4) Contracting: Marcus will provide cost delta to procurement and I will deliver the quote. Procurement please confirm lead time — target sign-off by 2026-06-18.

Action owners: 
- Infra/Provisioning (karthik.iyer@redwood.ai): confirm earliest provisioning date (estimate: 7 business days after sign-off).
- Deal ops (marcus.lin@redwood.ai): finalize cost delta and canary playbook.
- Sales (grace.oconnor@redwood.ai): finalize MOU language and send quote to procurement.

Simon — please confirm token mix and embedding concurrency by EOD 6/15 so we can finalize the quote.

Thanks all,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments referenced: initial-sizing-proposal.xlsx, latency-sla-matrix.pdf
